opening: Another name on an old family tree. What will this branch become?
reply: A shield for those who follow.
followup: Then carry more home than your scars.
closing: I will leave them a house that stands.

opening: Another name on an old family tree. What will this branch become?
reply: A record of what we learn here.
followup: Then carry more home than your scars.
closing: The next heir will have my notes.

opening: Another name on an old family tree. What will this branch become?
reply: A trail back to the people waiting for me.
followup: Then carry more home than your scars.
closing: I will mark the dangerous turns.

opening: Your family's banner again. Does each heir remember the climb?
reply: We remember the promises.
followup: Let memory guide you, but take your own steps.
closing: This oath is mine to keep.

opening: Your family's banner again. Does each heir remember the climb?
reply: We trade journals, including the mistakes.
followup: Let memory guide you, but take your own steps.
closing: I have room for another correction.

opening: Your family's banner again. Does each heir remember the climb?
reply: We learn the old tracks, then choose our route.
followup: Let memory guide you, but take your own steps.
closing: This trail still has surprises.

opening: You look like someone with an attic full of heirlooms. Anything interesting?
reply: Only this sword. I promised to bring it back.
followup: A family that keeps everything! We should get along.
closing: A gift would be easier to explain than a missing sword.

opening: You look like someone with an attic full of heirlooms. Anything interesting?
reply: My family keeps experiments in the attic.
followup: A family that keeps everything! We should get along.
closing: I could label anything you give me. For safety.

opening: You look like someone with an attic full of heirlooms. Anything interesting?
reply: Mostly maps and arrows with stories attached.
followup: A family that keeps everything! We should get along.
closing: Something light would fit beside the maps.

opening: More of that family! Did the last present make it home?
reply: Its story did. The armory remembers.
followup: Good. A proper collection needs a little excitement.
closing: I will try to bring back both this time.

opening: More of that family! Did the last present make it home?
reply: There is a detailed entry in the family journal.
followup: Good. A proper collection needs a little excitement.
closing: Preferably excitement that survives a jar.

opening: More of that family! Did the last present make it home?
reply: It left a mark on the trail.
followup: Good. A proper collection needs a little excitement.
closing: I am getting better at finding the way back.

opening: Come in, heir. Even an old family cannot climb on an empty stomach.
reply: I was taught to eat after everyone else.
followup: A place at the table is worth inheriting too.
closing: I suppose the others need me strong.

opening: Come in, heir. Even an old family cannot climb on an empty stomach.
reply: I packed books and forgot the provisions.
followup: A place at the table is worth inheriting too.
closing: I will add that to the packing list.

opening: Come in, heir. Even an old family cannot climb on an empty stomach.
reply: I have been living on whatever fits in my cloak.
followup: A place at the table is worth inheriting too.
closing: This smells much better than trail rations.

opening: Another of your house. I hope someone taught you to rest.
reply: They did. I am still learning to listen.
followup: Then take a little warmth with you for the climb.
closing: I will tell the next heir that rest is not surrender.

opening: Another of your house. I hope someone taught you to rest.
reply: The family journal now has a chapter on supper.
followup: Then take a little warmth with you for the climb.
closing: Some lessons deserve to be repeated.

opening: Another of your house. I hope someone taught you to rest.
reply: I know when a trail needs a campfire.
followup: Then take a little warmth with you for the climb.
closing: I will save the warmth for a cold stretch.

opening: A little heir with a long shadow. How much of your family do you carry?
reply: Their hopes are heavier than the armor.
followup: The tide keeps some things and returns others. Choose what you hold.
closing: I can put down the weight without dropping the promise.

opening: A little heir with a long shadow. How much of your family do you carry?
reply: Questions that have passed through many hands.
followup: The tide keeps some things and returns others. Choose what you hold.
closing: An unanswered question can still be a useful inheritance.

opening: A little heir with a long shadow. How much of your family do you carry?
reply: Their routes, their warnings, and a few knots.
followup: The tide keeps some things and returns others. Choose what you hold.
closing: I know which knots to loosen.

opening: Your house sends another traveler to the edge of the water.
reply: We are learning which burdens to leave behind.
followup: Then let this meeting be a new current, not an old anchor.
closing: I will carry what helps us stand.

opening: Your house sends another traveler to the edge of the water.
reply: The journals disagree about you.
followup: Then let this meeting be a new current, not an old anchor.
closing: I will leave room for a different answer.

opening: Your house sends another traveler to the edge of the water.
reply: The old tracks ended here, but mine can continue.
followup: Then let this meeting be a new current, not an old anchor.
closing: I will watch where the current bends.

opening: Your blood remembers shapes that your mind has forgotten. Will you change?
reply: I can change my stance without losing my oath.
followup: Growth does not ask the old branches for permission.
closing: Then I will learn to guard the new growth.

opening: Your blood remembers shapes that your mind has forgotten. Will you change?
reply: Inheritance is a beginning, not a finished formula.
followup: Growth does not ask the old branches for permission.
closing: I will observe carefully before calling it progress.

opening: Your blood remembers shapes that your mind has forgotten. Will you change?
reply: Every season changes the hunter and the trail.
followup: Growth does not ask the old branches for permission.
closing: I can follow a living trail.

opening: The family returns, and no two branches grow alike.
reply: We share a banner, not the same armor.
followup: Good. A bloodline should become more than its roots.
closing: There is room beneath it for someone different.

opening: The family returns, and no two branches grow alike.
reply: The differences are where the discoveries begin.
followup: Good. A bloodline should become more than its roots.
closing: I will write down what this branch learns.

opening: The family returns, and no two branches grow alike.
reply: The next heir may see tracks I miss.
followup: Good. A bloodline should become more than its roots.
closing: I will leave space for their path.

opening: Oh! A family hero! Is that your inherited look, or did you make it yourself?
reply: The dents in the armor are definitely mine.
followup: Then let us find something worthy of the family portrait!
closing: Preferably something that survives the next dent.

opening: Oh! A family hero! Is that your inherited look, or did you make it yourself?
reply: The hat is tradition. The scorch marks are new.
followup: Then let us find something worthy of the family portrait!
closing: I should take the portrait before the next experiment.

opening: Oh! A family hero! Is that your inherited look, or did you make it yourself?
reply: The cloak is old. I chose the feathers.
followup: Then let us find something worthy of the family portrait!
closing: A portrait is easier to carry than another cloak.

opening: A new face from the same splendid family! Shall we improve the collection?
reply: The armory has a shelf for the things we cannot wear.
followup: Wonderful! A family should never run out of beautiful stories.
closing: I will try to give this one a good ending.

opening: A new face from the same splendid family! Shall we improve the collection?
reply: The portrait gallery is becoming an excellent study of variation.
followup: Wonderful! A family should never run out of beautiful stories.
closing: And perhaps fewer scorch marks.

opening: A new face from the same splendid family! Shall we improve the collection?
reply: I have been collecting stories along the trail.
followup: Wonderful! A family should never run out of beautiful stories.
closing: I know a few worth bringing home.

opening: An heir! Show me what your family calls a weapon.
reply: A sword kept sharp through generations.
followup: Then find something here that deserves another story.
closing: The next heir should inherit a blade, not just a boast.

opening: An heir! Show me what your family calls a weapon.
reply: A staff, and the patience to aim it properly.
followup: Then find something here that deserves another story.
closing: I will test the grip before testing the explosion.

opening: An heir! Show me what your family calls a weapon.
reply: A bow that knows my hands, and arrows that do not come back.
followup: Then find something here that deserves another story.
closing: I will make the first shot count.

opening: Your family's weapons have found their way here again!
reply: We repair them between climbs.
followup: Good! An heir should learn a new trick before handing things down.
closing: I will make sure the lesson survives the battle.

opening: Your family's weapons have found their way here again!
reply: We improve the designs between disasters.
followup: Good! An heir should learn a new trick before handing things down.
closing: The family workshop could use a safer trick.

opening: Your family's weapons have found their way here again!
reply: We remember every shot that missed.
followup: Good! An heir should learn a new trick before handing things down.
closing: I have been saving a space in the quiver.

opening: You dress for a battle, but your family has sent you into a story.
reply: Then I will play the part that gets them home.
followup: Every house needs someone willing to step onto the stage.
closing: I can stand in the light without forgetting who is behind me.

opening: You dress for a battle, but your family has sent you into a story.
reply: I would rather understand the machinery behind the scenery.
followup: Every house needs someone willing to step onto the stage.
closing: I suppose someone must also take notes.

opening: You dress for a battle, but your family has sent you into a story.
reply: I prefer a quiet entrance and a clear exit.
followup: Every house needs someone willing to step onto the stage.
closing: I will keep an eye on the wings.

opening: Another heir takes the stage. Does your house know how this story ends?
reply: We know how to stand up after a bad ending.
followup: Then make the next scene worth remembering.
closing: I will give the next heir something to build on.

opening: Another heir takes the stage. Does your house know how this story ends?
reply: We have revised the ending several times.
followup: Then make the next scene worth remembering.
closing: This draft may still surprise us.

opening: Another heir takes the stage. Does your house know how this story ends?
reply: We know a few exits, and none of them are easy.
followup: Then make the next scene worth remembering.
closing: I will leave the trail visible.
